{"cc":[{"text":"Patient presents with right heel pain that has worsened over the past three weeks. She is also due to have a painful callus on her left plantar fifth metatarsal head pared.","start_char":116,"end_char":246}],"hpi":[{"text":"52-year-old female with no significant medical comorbidities reports right heel pain that began approximately three weeks ago after she increased her walking routine to prepare for a charity 5K. Pain is worst with the first steps in the morning and after prolonged sitting, classic post-static dyskinesia pattern. Pain is localized to the medial plantar heel, no radiation, no numbness. She has been using OTC ibuprofen with partial relief and has tried gel heel cups without significant improvement. Separately, she has a chronic intractable plantar keratoma at the left fifth metatarsal head that she has had debrided twice previously over the past year, most recently four months ago. The callus has rebuilt and is now painful with shoe wear.","start_char":248,"end_char":711}],"exam_findings":[{"text":"Vitals stable.
Right foot: tenderness localized to the medial calcaneal tubercle on direct palpation. Windlass test positive. No swelling, no erythema, no Achilles tenderness, no palpable mass. Range of motion at the ankle and subtalar joint within normal limits. Sensation grossly intact.
Left foot: discrete 8mm intractable plantar keratoma at the fifth metatarsal head with central nucleation, surrounding hyperkeratosis. No ulceration, no maceration, no signs of infection. The right foot shows no comparable lesions.
Both feet: pulses +2, capillary refill brisk, neurovascular intact otherwise.","start_char":713,"end_char":1085}],"mdm":[{"text":"Right heel pain is consistent with plantar fasciitis based on history and exam (post-static dyskinesia, positive Windlass test, medial calcaneal tubercle tenderness, recent activity increase). Differential includes calcaneal stress fracture given activity ramp-up, but absence of point tenderness on the calcaneal body and ability to bear weight makes this less likely. Plan: initiate plantar fasciitis protocol with night splint, calf and plantar fascia stretching, supportive footwear, and continued anti-inflammatory use. If no improvement in six weeks, will obtain weight-bearing X-rays to rule out heel spur or stress fracture and consider corticosteroid injection. Patient educated on expected timeline (8-12 weeks typical for resolution).

Separately, the left intractable plantar keratoma meets indication for paring given recurrence pattern, pain with weight bearing, and patient preference. Verified separate consent.","start_char":1087,"end_char":1555}],"procedure_note":[{"text":"Following informed consent specific to the paring procedure: left plantar fifth metatarsal head intractable keratoma was pared using sterile technique. Hyperkeratotic tissue removed sharply, central nucleation excised. No bleeding. Patient reported immediate relief.","start_char":1557,"end_char":1741}],"ambiguous_segments":[]}
